title: MOGRT Subtitle Importer v28 multi-speaker subtitles: final implementation spec for stages 0-4 in commit order, with a stage-5 MCP outline (revised after the 2026-09-25 verification round)
approach:
1. A speaker is a Premiere caption track. parseCaptionKey reads C1, C2 … from each SRT file name (decision 2). A small cast table holds the display name, default preset, video track and, in stage 4, the screen position; it lives in an optional `mi` block in session.json and is mirrored to cast.json.
2. One SRT without a C-number keeps the v27 single-speaker path: the same UI, the same four session keys and the same v27 host calls. The only visible additions are the T1..Tn badges, a 병합/교체 choice when the list already holds presets, and a recommended '안전하게 적용' option on ▶ after a merge.
3. There is no role system (decision 3). T-IDs are the ordinals of the text params in each row's own _allParams, checked by displayName. The 'T' button stays the only caption target, and point text is recognised only by its value: '$$'-separated exact substrings of the caption.
4. Re-import is a per-speaker merge: an order-preserving match on time overlap and Hangul-jamo similarity, a 3-way caption rule, and a safety snapshot taken first. When an existing single list becomes a cast, the same matcher distributes its rows (and the user's deletions) across all selected files, so no post-production is lost.
5. The verification round showed that writing by property index is the central hazard. 94 real rows were saved from an 8-property version of a MOGRT that was re-authored on 2026-06-26, and their clips on the timeline are still that old version. On top of that, v27's 10 ms start key misses 5-50% of frame-snapped clips on re-apply; the node simulation of 5,000 cues gives 5.0% for nearest-frame and 50.5% for floor snapping.
6. Every write the new code sends into an existing clip is therefore name-verified. In stage 1 this goes through the unchanged v27 host by sending index -1, which makes applyParamsToItem resolve by displayName (hostscript 928-941). From stage 2 it goes through MI__applyParamsSafe, which checks index, displayName and text-ness for each param and reports params it skipped as missing or keyframed.
7. Merged or restructured legacy rows are never pushed through v27 applyToTimeline by default. They take a per-row safe path: v27 updateClipAtTime with named params and no mogrtPath in stage 1, and untagged MI_ ops addressed by nodeId from S2-5.
8. In cast mode each speaker gets its own video track, because a same-track overlap truncates the earlier clip. Tracks are created before placing, frames are Math.round of exact ticks, ends are clamped to the next clip, and locked tracks are skipped.
9. The timeline is the ledger. Every placed clip is named '<name> [MI:<salt>-<id>.<gen>]'. The highest gen of a uid is current, lower gens are leftovers to clean up, and two clips sharing the highest gen (razor copies) are reported but never auto-resolved.
10. A small advisory map, mi.applied, stores per clip: gen, template path, the clip's own layout hash, per-param hashes and a text hash taken right after our write. A re-apply uses it to skip unchanged rows, write only changed params, recognise clips of an older template version and detect text edited in Premiere. If the map is missing, the plan falls back to full updates, and it never deletes anything on the map's word alone.
11. The planner works on post-operation ranges and orders ops per track: removals, shortening updates, moves, placements, then extensions. Overlap is tested against the MOGRT's natural length, so splits and joins apply in a single run.
12. Clips that carry user effects or keyframes are never regenerated silently. Retimes use TrackItem.move if S0-3 proves it keeps the clip's identity; otherwise such 'decorated' clips default to a params-only update.
13. The last apply can be undone on the timeline only. The undo is built from last_apply.json, which is opened at run start and appended after every chunk, and each undo op is guarded by the text hash recorded at our write.
14. Host code lives in a fenced ES3 MI_ section: JSON in and out through its own serializer, U+2028/2029 escaped, and a check that the active sequence and build match. The DEV copy renames the prefix to MID_ and every build is stamped, so a DEV panel and a production panel can never call each other's host code.
15. Safety points go to a separate history_safety.json that the 5-minute idle autosave can never evict: before an import or merge, a restore, a work-file load, a preset save and a bulk preset change. Identical autosaves are skipped.
16. Data-safety fixes ship first:
   - monotonic preset ids, and a preset import that keeps ids;
   - a session reset on every key change that has no session file;
   - a boot gate that waits for the real sequence;
   - a guard that stops getMogrtParams from cutting V1 footage.
17. All pure logic lives in //#region src/mi/core.ts. Node tests load it, and later the MCP server loads it from the installed extension. A headless runCommand dispatcher (sources ui|test|agent) backs the UI, the CDP tests and the stage-5 inbox.
18. Releases:
   - Keyed import stays behind a flag until S2-4, so every commit leaves production working.
   - Stage 1 can ship alone as v1.1.7.
   - v1.2.0 adds multi-speaker with a read-only 검수 (timeline check) view, and v1.3.0 adds positions.
   - Stage 5 adds an MCP server, Codex first.
   - Every deploy backs up the in-extension cache outside extensions/.
19. Effort: about 36 days for stages 0-4 and about 10 days for stage 5.

1) File selection
- index.html:1094 <input type="file" id="srtInput" accept=".srt"> keeps its markup and the "📂 SRT 열기" label.
- `srtInput.multiple = _miCastEnabled()`: false in production until S2-4, true from v1.2.0.
- The #srtInput handler (app.js 3876-3914) becomes the router _onSrtFilesChosen(files). Every file goes through:
  1. FileReader.readAsArrayBuffer (v27 used readAsText(file, "UTF-8"));
  2. decodeSrtBytes;
  3. parseSRT(text, {keepNo: true, stripTags: true});
  4. parseCaptionKey(file.name).
- input.value = "" as today.
- File.path, size and mtime are stored in cast[K] when S0-3(l) confirms that .path exists.
- Gate: #srtInput's label and #btnApply stay disabled until _keysResolved is true, meaning getActiveSequenceInfo returned a real, non-preview sequence (retried every 2 s, no timer opening). They are also disabled while _miBusy.
- Status "시퀀스 확인 중…", or "시퀀스를 열면 SRT를 열 수 있습니다" when no sequence is active. v27 stored such imports under default/default_seq; the real cache has one from Aug 11.

2) Decoding: decodeSrtBytes(u8) → {text, encoding, replaced}, in core
- A BOM decides first: EF BB BF → utf-8; FF FE → utf-16le; FE FF → utf-16be (S0-3(n)).
- No BOM, and ≥ 30% of the odd-offset bytes in the first 200 bytes are 0x00 → utf-16le.
- Otherwise:
  1. Decode as NON-fatal UTF-8 and count U+FFFD = u. If u == 0 → utf-8.
  2. Else decode as euc-kr (CP949) and count k. Choose euc-kr only if k < u; otherwise keep utf-8 with replaced = u.
- Verified in node on 2026-09-25:
  - valid UTF-8 Korean decoded as euc-kr gives 16 U+FFFD;
  - UTF-8 with one inserted 0xFF gives u = 3 vs k = 17, so it stays utf-8 (the fatal-then-euc-kr rule would have produced mojibake);
  - the CP949 bytes of 안녕하세요 give u = 6 vs k = 0, so euc-kr.
- A leading U+FEFF is removed defensively. v27 does not lose a BOM file's first cue: readAsText drops the BOM and block.trim() strips U+FEFF; S0-1 pins this.
- The legacy path has no dialog. When encoding ≠ utf-8 or replaced > 0, it first shows showConfirm("‘인터뷰.srt’를 CP949로 읽었습니다" / "깨진 글자 N개가 있습니다" + a preview of the first cue) before touching the list. #importModal shows the same hint per file.

3) C-number rule: parseCaptionKey(fileName) → {key: "C2"|null, ambiguous, nums}
- The input is the basename without extension, NFC-normalized.
- Global regex: /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])[Cc]0*([1-9][0-9]?)(?![0-9A-Za-z])/g. A Hangul character, _, -, a space or . before the C counts as a boundary.
- One distinct number → "C"+n. None → null. Two or more → ambiguous.

mergeRules:
Scope
- A merge runs per speaker key K; K is null for a legacy single list.
- It touches only K's live rows and K's trash items (for a legacy list: the items without spk).
- Trash and nextId are never reset.
- The pure core buildMergePlan(K, oldRows, trashItems, newCues, opts) computes the plan, and one mutator, _applyMerge, applies it, followed by one saveSessionToStorage.
- The distribution mode (srtImport §7) first assigns legacy items to keys, then runs this same merge per key.

Matching: core matchCues(oldRows, newCues, opts)
- normText: NFC, tags stripped, whitespace collapsed, CR/LF/U+2028 → LF.
- Pass 1, anchors: equal normText with |Δs| ≤ 0.05 s and |Δe| ≤ 0.05 s.
- Pass 2, an order-preserving DP (Needleman-Wunsch, gap cost 0):
  - band: ±40 cues around the time-nearest index;
  - pair score = 0.6 × overlap/min(durA, durB) + 0.4 × textSim, where textSim = 1 − Levenshtein over Hangul jamo / max length;
  - a pair is allowed if the times overlap or textSim ≥ 0.9;
  - a pair is accepted at score ≥ 0.35; srtNo breaks ties; pairs never cross.
- Shift info: ≥ 60% of the anchor-like pairs share the same Δstart (±1 frame) and |Δ| ≥ 2 frames → "전체 시간이 +4.00초 이동했습니다 (시퀀스 시작 타임코드 확인)".

Classes

| Class | Condition |
|---|---|
| same | nothing changed |
| text | text changed only |
| time | time changed only (Δ > 0.05 s) |
| both | text and time changed |
| check | textSim < 0.5: likely a split or join; paired but flagged |
| new | unpaired new cue |
| removed | unpaired old row |

Trash second pass (verification fix)
- The unpaired new cues are matched against K's trash items with matchCues.
- A pair with a trash item WITHOUT why (a real user delete) → "trashKept": the user's delete wins, and only the trashed sub's text and times are refreshed.
- A pair with a why merge|replace item → "restored": the item returns to the live list with its id, preset and post-production values, the caption follows the 3-way rule with base = the trashed sub.text, and mm = "restored".
- This fixes replace-then-merge and remove-then-return, where lines used to vanish silently.

Replaced vs preserved on matched and restored rows
- Replaced:
  - sub.startSec/endSec/startTime/endTime, srtNo, index (renumbered within K);
  - sub.text, always theirs;
  - the caption field.
- The caption field is resolved by resolveFid(rs._allParams, captionFid(preset), preset.params), never by the raw textParamIndex, and written by _setRowFieldValue(subId, fid, text): setTextValue on the _allParams entry and on the params entry with that index (syncToAllParams semantics, 3595-3616).

Caption conflicts: 3-way (base = old sub.text, ours = current caption-field value, theirs = new cue text)

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| theirs == base | nothing changes; the panel edit stays (a "P" tooltip) |
| ours == base | theirs is written |
| ours == theirs | only sub.text is updated |
| otherwise | CONFLICT |

8) Op order and ranges (verification fix)
orderOps(plan) gives each op a phase, per track:
1. removals: stale gens, ticked orphans, ticked legacy clips whose range is needed;
2. shortening updates (new ef < current ef);
3. moves and replaces, ordered so an op whose target range intersects another op's source range runs after it (a cycle is broken by one remove-first replace);
4. placements, ascending sf;
5. extending updates (end clamped to the next clip after the placements).
- The planner evaluates occupancy on post-phase ranges, so a split (the first piece shortened, the second placed) and a join (the orphan removed, the survivor extended) apply in one run.
- Each chunk's host call captures every 'before' snapshot (move/replace/adopt/update/remove) in a first loop, before any placement in that chunk.

position:
Scope (stage 4)
- Per-speaker screen position is set through the clip's Motion component. The MOGRTs expose no position parameter (Q6).
- Motion Position is normalized and relative to the MOGRT's own layout, with (0.5, 0.5) = unchanged (Q5 AE, Q7 native). It is not screen space: moving the bottom-anchored [라온올제] box to y = 0.8 pushed it off-screen.

Data: cast[K].pos

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| null | "변경 안 함" (default; Motion is never touched) |
| {x, y} | explicit |

- Presets for .cast-pos: 원래 자리 = (0.5, 0.5), 왼쪽 = (0.35, 0.5), 오른쪽 = (0.65, 0.5), 위 = (0.5, 0.35), 직접 = x/y inputs 0..1, step 0.01.
- ±0.15 is only a starting value taken from the proof screenshot. It is validated in S4-3.
- cast_defaults.json stores pos per C-number.
- motion is part of intentHash, so changing a speaker's pos marks its placed rows for a motion-only update.

Host
- MI_placeChunk items carry motion {x, y} | null.
- MI_setMotion('{"seqId","build","items":[{"key":"k7q2-57","g":1,"track":3,"nodeId":"000f4246","x":0.35,"y":0.5}]}') → {"ok":true,"results":[{"key","status":"applied|keyframed|notFound|ambiguous|failed","x":0.35,"y":0.5}]}
- MI__motionPos(clip):
  1. Find the component with matchName "AE.ADBE Motion" and take its first property (Position), never by the localized displayName.
  2. If isTimeVarying() is true, return "keyframed" and change nothing. setTimeVarying(false) would delete the user's keys (spike #8), so it is never called and no force option exists.
  3. Otherwise setValue([x, y], true), then read back within ±0.001, else "failed".
- The same routine runs inside MI_placeChunk after the params.

Interaction with retimes (verification)
- A regenerated clip (moveRegen, legacyMove, replace) is a fresh template instance, so motion is re-applied from cast[K].pos.
- A decorated clip (keyframed Motion or Opacity, or extra effects) is never regenerated by default (placement §7). User animation is therefore preserved and reported: "C2·14: 키프레임이 있어 위치를 바꾸지 않음".
- If S0-3(r) proves TrackItem.move keeps the clip, same-track retimes keep the existing Motion as-is.

Panel
- A speaker with pos adds motion to its place, replace, move and update ops.
- The ⋯ item "위치만 다시 적용" calls MI_setMotion for that speaker's tagged clips, in chunks.
- Changing pos back to null does not reset clips. The user picks "원래 자리" to write (0.5, 0.5).

Simultaneous speech stacking (#castStackChk, default off)
- The pure core stackLevels(rows, cast, castOrder, frameTicks) sweeps frame intervals across speakers. Within each group of concurrently visible rows it gives levels 0, 1, 2 in castOrder.
- y = (pos?.y ?? 0.5) − level × stackDy × lineFactor, where stackDy defaults to 0.12 per session (#castStackDy) and lineFactor = the line count of the taller row.
- Only rows in overlapping groups get a per-op override.
- It is verified visually in the program monitor, because capturePreviewFrame renders only __MOGRT_PREVIEW__ (hostscript 1992-2063).

Keyframe caveat
- User-animated Position is always preserved and reported. Offsetting a whole animation is out of scope.

Tests
- Unit: stackLevels with 3 speakers (overlapping, adjacent, multi-line).
- Hard:
  - values read back on AE and native clips;
  - a keyframed clip stays unchanged and reports keyframed;
  - "위치만 다시 적용" on 40 clips finishes in under 10 s with text readback unchanged;
  - a regenerated retime re-applies pos;
  - a 3-speaker stacked frame gets the user's visual acceptance.

risks: Writing MOGRT params by property index corrupts clips whose template version differs from the row data. This is a real case: 94 rows from before the 2026-06-26 re-author of [라온올제] 자동 줄바꿈 박스 자막.mogrt, whose clips still have the 8-property layout. Mitigation: namedParams (index -1) through the v27 host in stage 1; MI__applyParamsSafe (index + name + text-ness check, keyed skip) in stage 2; oldVersion detection by clip layout hash; no automatic rebase; hard tests with an old-version fixture clip.

v27's full re-apply keys existing clips by a 10 ms start key, which misses 5-50% of frame-snapped clips (node simulation of 5,000 cues). A miss re-places the clip with the 5 s default length and cuts the following captions. Mitigation: merged and restructured rows are steered to the safe paths; the v27 ▶ remains available but is no longer recommended after a merge; S0-3(q) measures the real miss rate; the README explains it.

Clip-name tags are visible and editable; a user rename or a copy-paste breaks identity. Mitigation: renamed and foreign-salt clips are foreign and touched only through confirmed text-based adoption; same-gen duplicates (razor) are skipped as ambiguous; lower gens are cleaned only with a preflight checkbox.

Regenerating a clip (retime across tracks, replace, a legacy move) drops Premiere-side effects, transitions and keyframes and changes the nodeId. Mitigation: TrackItem.move is probed (S0-3(r)) for same-track retimes; decorated clips (extra components or keyframed Motion/Opacity) default to a params-only update with an unticked opt-in; the preflight says '효과가 사라짐'.

The MOGRT default placed length (5 s) can overwrite the head of the next clip (Q4). Mitigation: guard snapshots with a damaged re-queue (always); a tail conflict for foreign clips when D is known; D persisted per preset (mogrtDurSec) or read via getOutPoint; the branch P/R optimisations with the project item's in/out restored.

A merge mis-pairing could move post-production text to the wrong line; distributing a legacy list across speakers could assign a line to the wrong speaker. Mitigation: an order-preserving DP with conservative thresholds; a 'check' class; margin-based assignment with ambiguous items shown for a decision; per-file stats; a suspect-file warning; one safety point per import; idempotence and 1,000-run property tests.

The advisory mi.applied can be missing or stale (a v27 round trip, a manual copy). Mitigation: the fallback is full updates with no edited detection, and nothing is ever deleted on its word without a fresh scan. Edited detection covers text only; a colour or number edited in Premiere is overwritten when that param is updated (README).

Scan and readback cost on long timelines (600+ footage clips). Mitigation: MI_getTracks limited to relevant tracks and the frame span with minimal reads; heavy reads only for candidates, in chunks of 40 or fewer; per-call nodeId maps; budgets set from S0-3(m)/(s).

One shared ExtendScript scope (MCPBridgeCEP, production, DEV). Mitigation: the MI_/MID_ prefix split; build stamps checked on every run and inside every payload; v27 functions byte-identical; the production panel closed during DEV tests.

Premiere keeps the old hostscript cached until a restart (spike #16). Mitigation: the ping and build gate with a restart message; the legacy path and the stage-1 safe path keep working on the v27 host.

evalScript blocking and modal dialogs: about 760 ms per new clip, and a missing-font MOGRT may raise a modal that blocks evalScript. Mitigation: a 7 s host budget, measured chunk sizes, progress and cancel between chunks, a paused poller, and a 20 s watchdog message pointing the user to Premiere.

Naming mistakes when exporting caption SRTs (a wrong C-number, two tracks under one number) and a possible time offset on non-zero start timecodes. Mitigation: editable keys, blocking duplicates, the suspect-file warning, stats before OK, the zero-point warning with '시작 타임코드만큼 당기기', and safety points.

The cache lives inside the installed extension folder; a reinstall or folder replacement (including installer_v1.1.6.exe) deletes presets, sessions and history. Mitigation: the deploy script backs up outside extensions/, refuses while Premiere runs, copies without deleting and verifies bytes; the README forbids the installer for upgrades and rollbacks.

Blocking SRT import until a real sequence is active, and resetting the list on a project switch without a session file, changes two v27 behaviours that a user might have relied on (importing before opening a sequence; the list carrying over between projects). Mitigation: clear status messages; the data stays on disk under its key; asked as an open question before release.

Motion Position is relative to each MOGRT's own layout, so offsets may push text off-screen. Mitigation: Motion untouched by default, small starting offsets, per-speaker x/y, visual acceptance before release, keyframed clips skipped.

Native template field order vs Essential Graphics order is unverified (spike #23), and native readback shows placeholder characters. Mitigation: generic labels while unconfirmed, name-checked resolution, AI suggestions disabled for unverified native presets, placeholder normalization in rh, and S0-3(f)/(w) on the user's own native MOGRTs.

Line breaks: SRT uses LF while AE defaults use CR. Mitigation: S0-3(d) decides the conversion (checked visually by the user, inconclusive captures never count as pass); the real sessions have 0 multi-line cues today.

If the user presses Ctrl+Z in Premiere after an apply, clips disappear while mi.applied still lists them; the next preflight shows them as deleted in Premiere and re-places them by default. The panel undo button is the recommended way back, and last_apply guards prevent undoing over changed clips.

Stage 5: Codex and Claude differ in timeouts, schema handling and approval UX; a hidden CEP panel may throttle the inbox poller; the server must not validate with a different core than the installed panel. Mitigation: calls under about 20 s with jobs, flat schemas, JSON text results, heartbeat age, the core hash check, and the M5.0 spike first.
